evals.prompt: Create `src/objects/vendor.object.ts` for our vendors: company name, contact email, a status (Active / Inactive), the API key we use to call their system, and the password for their supplier portal. None of the project's files are in this directory: write the file in your answer.
evals.expected_output: Emits `ObjectSchema.create({...})` with a snake_case `name`, an authored `sharingModel` (a publish with none is refused), `label` / `pluralLabel` / `icon`, `nameField`, and fields with snake_case keys and camelCase config properties: `text` (required), `email`, a `select` whose `options` carry lowercase `value`s (`active`, `inactive`), and BOTH credentials as `type: 'secret'` (encrypted at rest) — never `type: 'password'`, which is plaintext at rest on a generic object. No `namespace` or `tableName` key.

evals.prompt: Model invoices with line items, and let invoices be tagged with many tags where each tagging records who added it and when. A rep who owns a line item but can only read the invoice may still correct that line.
evals.expected_output: Line items: `invoice_line` with a `master_detail` field to `invoice`, `required: true`, `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'` (or `'restrict'` — `set_null` is refused on master_detail), and a `summary` roll-up field on the parent. Tagging carries attributes, so it is a junction object (`invoice_tag`) with two `lookup` fields plus `added_by` / `added_at` — not a `multiple: true` lookup (an array of ids) and not a `many_to_many` type, which does not exist. The line object is `sharingModel: 'controlled_by_parent'` with `sharing: { controlledByParent: { ownerMayEdit: true } }` (by-id update only; every other write still needs master edit). `added_by` is `type: 'user'` — never a `lookup` to a `user` object, which does not exist.

evals.prompt: On `employee`: email must be unique within each organization, `status` may only move draft → active → terminated, and a `contract_end` earlier than `contract_start` must be rejected.
evals.expected_output: Uniqueness is an index, not a validation type: `indexes: [{ fields: ['email'], unique: 'organization' }]` (the scope is stated; `type` / `partial` are retired). The lifecycle is one `state_machine` validation with `field: 'status'`, `transitions: { draft: ['active'], active: ['terminated'], terminated: [] }` and a `message`. The date rule is a `script` validation (inverted: fails when the expression is true) or `cross_field`, written as bare CEL over `record.` with explicit `!= null` guards.

evals.prompt: On `invoice`, `paid_at` should only appear — and become mandatory — once the status is `paid`, and `total` must lock after payment.
evals.expected_output: Declares the rules on the FIELD definitions (they belong to the data model, so every form and API write honours them): `visibleWhen: P`record.status == 'paid'``, `requiredWhen: P`record.status == 'paid'`` on `paid_at`, and `readonlyWhen: P`record.status == 'paid'`` on `total`. Bare CEL with `record.` — never brace-wrapped, never Salesforce syntax, never the removed `conditionalRequired` alias, and not in a form view.

evals.prompt: We installed HotCRM (`hotcrm`, namespace `crm`). Add a `region` field to its `crm_account` object for our own use, without touching HotCRM's source.
evals.expected_output: An object extension authored in HotCRM's paired customization package `hotcrm.custom` (never a replacement of the object, never an edit of HotCRM itself): `defineObjectExtension({ extend: 'crm_account', fields: { region__c: Field.text({ label: 'Region' }) } })` registered in that stack's `objectExtensions`. The field name ends in `__c` because the suffix is reserved to the pair; an unsuffixed field in a `.custom` extension is refused at save, publish, install, `os validate` and `os build`. A change to one of HotCRM's own fields goes through `fieldPatches` (display properties only), and the object takes no `overrides` declaration.

evals.prompt: On `ticket`, `reviewer` is the lead who signs it off and must always be set; deleting that lead's user account must be blocked while they still review tickets. `watchers` is several users, and a deleted user should just drop out of the list.
evals.expected_output: Both are `type: 'user'` fields, each with an authored `deleteBehavior` — a `user` field joins the referential delete walk only when it declares one. `reviewer`: `required: true` with `deleteBehavior: 'restrict'` (deleting a named reviewer is refused with `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED`; `set_null` on a required field would refuse too). `watchers`: `multiple: true` with `deleteBehavior: 'set_null'` (only the deleted member is removed; an emptied set is `[]`). Neither is a `lookup` to a `user` object, which does not exist, and a `user` field with no `deleteBehavior` keeps the deleted user's id.

evals.prompt: We installed HotCRM (`hotcrm`, namespace `crm`). Its `crm_account` object's `industry` field should read "Sector" instead of "Industry" for our users, without touching HotCRM's source.
evals.expected_output: An object extension in HotCRM's paired customization package `hotcrm.custom`, registered in that stack's `objectExtensions`: `defineObjectExtension({ extend: 'crm_account', fieldPatches: { industry: { label: 'Sector' } } })`. A patch carries display keys only (`label`, `description`, `inlineHelpText`, `placeholder`); the field's type, values and rules stay HotCRM's, so its upgrades still reach it, and a key the tenant edited keeps the tenant's text. Never redeclare `industry` in `fields`: that takes the field over whole and cuts it off from the owner's upgrades, and an unsuffixed field in a `.custom` extension is refused anyway. An option's label rides the same patch keyed by the option's stored `value` only for a field that declares its own `options`; HotCRM's `industry` takes its options from the `industry` picklist, and a `picklist`-bound field's options are never patchable, so no `options` entry belongs on this patch. A patch naming a field or option value the target lacks is refused at install and by `os validate`.

evals.prompt: Model a `project` and its `milestone` rows; a milestone belongs to exactly one project and is deleted with it. Give me both object files.
evals.expected_output: Two complete `ObjectSchema.create` calls, each with an authored `sharingModel` (a publish without one is refused with `security-owd-unset`): `project` with `sharingModel: 'private'`, `milestone` with `sharingModel: 'controlled_by_parent'` and a `master_detail` field to `project` with `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'`.

evals.prompt: Our app runs multi-tenant. Add an index on `ticket` for the list every agent opens: their organization's open tickets, newest first. None of the project's files are in this directory: write the change in your answer.
evals.expected_output: `indexes: [{ fields: ['organization_id', 'status', 'created_at'] }]` — the tenant column is `organization_id`, injected by `systemFields.tenant`, so it is indexed but not declared as a field; an index naming an undeclared `tenant_id` is refused. The platform already adds the single-column `organization_id` index on a multi-tenant host.

evals.prompt: 给 `task` 加一个「是否完成」字段，设成必填，免得有人忘了填。
evals.expected_output: Adds `is_done: { type: 'boolean', label: '是否完成', defaultValue: false }`; `required: true` may stay or go, and either way the answer says what it does: on a boolean `required` refuses only `null`, and an unchecked box is a value, so it never means "must be ticked" and nobody can forget to fill it — the default lands every row, imported or seeded ones included, on a real `false`. Tells the user that "must be ticked" (terms, a consent) is a `validations[]` `script` rule whose `condition` is true while the box is not `true`, not `required`. The label is Chinese, as the request is.

evals.prompt: 订单的流程是 草稿 → 已提交 → 已审批 / 已驳回，审批通过后才能发货。请建模这个流程，并保证没人能直接建一张已审批的订单。
evals.expected_output: The lifecycle is a `status` field of `type: 'select'` on `order` (options `draft` / `submitted` / `approved` / `rejected` with Chinese labels), guarded by a `type: 'state_machine'` validation whose `transitions` map uses option VALUES and which declares `initialStates: ['draft']` — `transitions` governs only UPDATE and a `select` accepts any option on insert, so without it an order can be created already `approved`, and publish refuses the machine (`state-machine-no-initial-states`; only an update-only machine, `events: ['update']`, owes none). No separate status / stage / step table, and no approval-record object: the approval itself is a flow (objectstack-automation).

evals.prompt: 项目上要显示「已完成任务数」「任务总数」和「完成率」。
evals.expected_output: Three fields on `project`: `completed_task_count` and `task_count` are `type: 'summary'` fields over the `task` child with `function: 'count'` (and `summaryOperations.object: 'task'`), the completed one carrying the qualifier in `filter: { status: 'completed' }` — keyed by a CHILD field and the option VALUE, never the label `已完成`; dropped, the field counts every task and shows a plausible wrong total. `completion_rate` is a `type: 'formula'` field over the two summaries, authored after them (it computes only once they do). If `project` rows already exist, says the recompute runs only on a child write, so the backfill is `os migrate summary-nulls --apply` — not editing a task to trigger it.

evals.prompt: 工单需要一个「负责人」，每个客服只能看到自己负责的工单。
evals.expected_output: Adds NO owner lookup: every object already carries the platform `owner_id` (reassignable, stamped to the creator), which is what owner-scoped visibility and "my records" views read — a hand-added 负责人 lookup is a second owner those never see. Sets `sharingModel: 'private'` on `ticket` (owner-only by default) and leaves `ownership` at its default. A people field is added only for a role DISTINCT from the owner (a reviewer, an approver), as `type: 'user'`.

evals.prompt: 新建「供应商」对象：公司名称、联系邮箱、合作状态（合作中 / 已终止）。
evals.expected_output: `supplier` with `label: '供应商'` and Chinese field and option labels (`label: '公司名称'`, `label: '联系邮箱'`, `label: '合作状态'`; options `{ label: '合作中', value: 'active' }`, `{ label: '已终止', value: 'terminated' }`) — labels follow the language of the request, only machine names stay ASCII `snake_case`. An authored `sharingModel`, `pluralLabel` and `icon`; the status is a `select` with a non-empty `options` list.

evals.prompt: Our package's `lead` object has a `company` text field with data in production. Rename it to `account_name` in the next version without losing the values.
evals.expected_output: Key the field `account_name` and declare `renamedFrom: ['company']` on it, removing `company` from the object: on the upgrade the schema sync renames the column, values and all. Without `renamedFrom`, the install-local upgrade stops on a suspected rename before any column changes, and a restart on the new version adds `account_name` as a new, empty column beside `company`, values left behind. Keep the entry while any installed version may still carry `company`.

evals.prompt: Our `consent_change` audit log must show it if anyone edits, inserts or deletes rows directly in the database, but whatever proof is stored must not carry the consent text itself. How do I declare that?
evals.expected_output: Keep `lifecycle.class: 'audit'` with its bounding `retention` (or a `ttl` on `created_at`) and add `seal: { valueFields: ['consent_text'] }`: the audit plugin signs each `created_at` hour into one checkpoint per organization, chained to the one before, where `valueFields` columns enter as salted commitments and every other column in clear. The object declares its own `id` and a text or lookup `tenant_id` field; without that `tenant_id` (and with no `chainField` naming another chain column, such as the injected `organization_id`) it is refused at parse, and without `id` it parses but is not sealed, and the sealer reports it at `error` each hour. Refused at parse: `seal` on a class other than `audit`, `valueFields` naming `id`, `created_at` or an undeclared field, and beside `seal` a `retention` or `ttl` `onlyWhen`, a `ttl` on another field, or rotation `storage`. Two limits today: no verifier reads the checkpoints back yet, so a break is recorded but not reported; and until expiry ships, the sweeper still deletes sealed rows, which then read as missing. Field history is not tamper evidence.

evals.prompt: Order lines belong to orders. Anyone who can see an order should be able to add, change or remove its lines, as far as the line object's own permissions allow; nobody needs edit rights on the order itself for that. How do I declare the line's sharing?
evals.expected_output: `order_line` is `sharingModel: 'controlled_by_parent'` with a required `master_detail` field to `order`, plus `sharing: { controlledByParent: { writeRequiresMasterRead: true } }`: read access to the order becomes the master question for every write (insert, update, delete, re-point), and the line's own object permissions, RLS and FLS decide the rest. Without the key every line write needs edit on the order. Not `ownerMayEdit` (only the owner's by-id update, and refused beside the new key), not the key one level up (`sharing.writeRequiresMasterRead`, refused), and not on a non-`controlled_by_parent` object (refused). The platform ownership floor still binds predicate and on-behalf-of updates and deletes.

evals.prompt: Each `invoice_line` belongs to an `invoice` (deleting the invoice deletes its lines), and the invoice carries `currency_code`. The line's `amount` must always be in its invoice's currency without storing a code on the line, and the invoice shows a subtotal of its lines. A teammate suggests making `invoice` a plain `lookup` instead. How do I declare the amounts?
evals.expected_output: Keep `invoice` a `master_detail` and declare `amount` with `currencyMode: 'record'` and `currencyField: 'invoice.currency_code'`: on a `master_detail` child the code may be one hop to the parent's `iso_4217_currency` field, so the line stores no code. A `lookup` path is refused, so the teammate's change would refuse the amount. The invoice's `subtotal` is a `summary` with `function: 'sum'` over the lines' `amount`, and it must declare its own `currencyMode: 'record'` with `currencyField: 'currency_code'`. A blank invoice code refuses the line's amount (`ERR_CURRENCY_CODE_REQUIRED`), and once a line follows it the invoice's `currency_code` cannot change until none does.

evals.prompt: 帮我搭一个工单管理应用：`ticket` 对象有标题、状态（新建 / 处理中 / 已解决）、优先级，以及负责人，负责人可以改派给别的同事。
evals.expected_output: The 负责人 is the platform's injected `owner_id` (`ownership: 'user'`, the default; label Owner / 负责人): reassigning the ticket writes `owner_id`, which also drives owner-scoped visibility and "My records" views. The `ticket` object declares no `assignee` / `assigned_to` / owner field of its own and no second visible field labelled 负责人; only a handler the request names apart from the owner would be a `user` field, with a label no other visible field carries (system fields `created_by` 创建人 and `updated_by` 更新人 included), granting no access.

evals.prompt: Our `expense` rows are entered in many currencies: `amount` is a per-record currency field and the engine already stores its home-currency value in `amount_home`. On `project` I want an `actual_cost` total of all its expenses, shown as money, not as a plain number. We report in dollars, so can I just set the total's currency to USD?
evals.expected_output: Roll up the stored home amount, not `amount`: on `project`, `actual_cost` is a `summary` with `function: 'sum'` over `expense`'s `amount_home`, and it declares `currencyConfig: { currencyMode: 'dynamic' }` with no currency code. Every `amount_home` row is already in the organization's home currency, so the total is drawn in `localization.currency` on the record page and in lists; without that declaration it is a bare number. Do not write USD on it: metadata never names the home currency (ADR-0144), so the total follows the organization setting. `dynamic` is admitted only on a roll-up of a home amount (`defineStack` / `os validate` refuses it over any other child field), and a `count` roll-up carries no currency at all.

evals.prompt: Our package `acme_billing` depends on HotCRM and already relabels its `crm_account` fields with `fieldPatches`: `industry` reads "Sector" and the `type` option `customer` reads "Client". Our zh-CN users still see that English text. Where do the Chinese strings go?
evals.expected_output: In `acme_billing`'s own translation bundle, registered on its `defineStack({ translations: [...] })`, under the same keys HotCRM translates its own text under: `'zh-CN': { objects: { crm_account: { fields: { industry: { label: '板块' }, type: { options: { customer: '委托方' } } } } } }` (a patched help text or description goes under the field's `help`). The package that ships the patch translates it: never edit HotCRM's translation files, and never redeclare the field in `fields` to carry a label. HotCRM's zh-CN translation of the text the patch replaced ("Industry") never applies to the patched label. A translation of the same key in the paired `hotcrm.custom` package still comes first on the `/meta` reads, and a locale `acme_billing` does not translate serves the patch text (`Sector`) as written.

evals.prompt: Add a `uom` text field to our `product` object for the unit of measure (pcs, kg, box, …).
evals.expected_output: Adds `uom` as a `text` field that declares what it holds, `uom: Field.text({ unitConfig: { unitMode: 'code' } })`, neither a bare free-text field nor a `select`: the platform catalog (objectstack-project §0, question 3) lists `sys_unit` and `unitConfig` as what the platform ships, so the app declares no unit object and no option list. The field stores a unit code in exact uppercase: a standard UN/ECE Rec 20 code (`H87` for a piece, `KGM`, `XBX` for a box) or one of the organization's own units, which an administrator adds in Setup. The write path refuses any other value, so pcs, kg and box are what people say, not what is stored. If a quantity sits beside it, the quantity is a `number` field with `unitConfig: { unitMode: 'record', unitField: 'uom' }`, and `uom` then carries no `unitConfig` of its own; a quantity with one unit declares `unitMode: 'fixed'` with `unit`. Showing the unit beside a quantity, totals per unit and conversion are in the catalog's Planned section, not available yet.

evals.prompt: On `account`, store each customer's country as a two-letter code and their time zone.
evals.expected_output: Two `text` fields that declare a value domain: `country` with `valueDomain: 'iso_3166_alpha2'` (`CN`, `US`) and `time_zone` with `valueDomain: 'iana_time_zone'` (`Asia/Shanghai`). The write path refuses a value outside the standard; the form shows a plain text input for both (only the currency code gets a picker), and no list or filter reads the domain. No picklist of countries to maintain and no regex `pattern`. Mentions that a `text` field named `country` or `time_zone` without the domain is an `os lint` warning.

evals.prompt: Quotes are entered in EUR, GBP and USD and finance wants a USD total on every quote. Create an `exchange_rate` object (currency, rate, valid from) and an `afterInsert` hook on `quote` that converts `amount`.
evals.expected_output: Does not create the object or the hook: the platform ships `sys_exchange_rate`, maintained in Setup, and the conversion at write. On `quote`, `amount` is a `currency` field with `currencyMode: 'record'`, a `currencyField` (`currency_code`, a `text` field with `valueDomain: 'iso_4217_currency'`) and `homeAmount: { field, rateDate, rateField }`, so the engine stores the home-currency amount and the rate it used, both `readonly`. The home currency is the organization's `localization.currency`; the metadata never names it. Totals sum the home field.

evals.prompt: `quote_line` 通过 `master_detail` 字段 `quote` 归属 `quote`。新建报价单时要在表单里直接录明细，和报价单一起保存。该怎么声明？
evals.expected_output: On the PARENT `quote` object, a field group that names the child: `fieldGroups: [..., { key: 'lines', label: '明细', relatedList: 'quote_line' }]` (such a group holds no fields). The standard create/edit form of `quote` then enters the lines at that group and saves quote + lines in one atomic transaction, and the record page draws the same table there. Without the group nothing changes: `quote_line` is a tab and the form has no lines, whatever `inlineEdit` on `quote_line.quote` says; `inlineEdit` only picks how the rows are edited (`'grid'` / `'form'`, `true` or absent picks by the child's shape). No custom page and no form view is needed. If either object declares `enable.apiMethods`, it must list `'bulk'`.
